# AGENTS.md instructions for /work

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [14]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

Scenario ID: SCN-015
Title: Remove the final tag without changing the bookmark
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-015
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

A bookmark is allowed to have no tags. Removing its final tag leaves its title, description, source, image, address, and other details untouched. When no bookmarks use the removed tag, that tag also disappears from the sidebar instead of remaining as an empty entry.

## Gherkin

Feature: Remove bookmark tags

  Scenario: Remove a bookmark's only tag
    Given a bookmark has exactly one tag
    And no other bookmarks use that tag
    When the user removes the tag
    And saves the tag changes
    Then the bookmark has no tags
    And all non-tag bookmark details remain unchanged
    And the unused tag no longer appears in the sidebar

## Assumptions

- Tags do not exist independently once no bookmarks use them.
- A bookmark does not require at least one tag.

## Related scenarios

- SCN-004

# AGENTS.md instructions for /work

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [15]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

# AGENTS.md instructions for /work

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [16]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

# AGENTS.md instructions for /work

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [17]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

Scenario ID: SCN-018
Title: Require a title while allowing an empty description
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-018
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

A bookmark must have a non-empty title so that it remains recognizable, while its description may be empty. If the client tries to save corrected details without a title, the editor stays open, explains that a title is required, and leaves the existing saved bookmark unchanged. Once a title is provided, the correction can be saved even with an empty description.

## Gherkin

Feature: Correct bookmark details

  Scenario: Reject corrected details with no title
    Given a saved bookmark has existing details
    And the user has opened its details editor
    When the user clears the title
    And tries to save the changes
    Then the editor remains open
    And a message says that a title is required
    And the saved bookmark remains unchanged

  Scenario: Save a title with no description
    Given the user is editing a bookmark's details
    When the user enters a non-empty title
    And leaves the description empty
    And saves the changes
    Then the bookmark shows the new title
    And the bookmark has no description

## Assumptions

- Title is required for recognition and search.
- Description is optional.

## Related scenarios

- SCN-002

# AGENTS.md instructions for /work

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [18]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

Scenario ID: SCN-021
Title: Keep the saved copy unchanged when the original page changes
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-021
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

A saved page copy remains frozen as the version captured on the original save date, even if the live webpage changes later. The captured content is never silently refreshed or replaced. Choosing Try original page opens the current live version separately, allowing the client to compare it without affecting the dependable saved snapshot.

## Gherkin

Feature: Preserve saved pages over time

  Scenario: Keep the captured version after the original changes
    Given a readable copy of a webpage was captured on the bookmark's save date
    And the original webpage changes later
    When the user opens the saved bookmark
    Then the saved reading page shows the version captured on the save date
    And the saved copy is not silently updated from the live page
    When the user chooses "Try original page"
    Then the current live webpage opens separately
    And the saved copy remains unchanged

## Assumptions

- Saved page copies are immutable snapshots unless a future explicitly approved behavior says otherwise.
- Opening the live original never overwrites the saved copy.

# AGENTS.md instructions for /work

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [21]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

+Title: Archive a bookmark that is still in Read later
+Type: Edge Case

+Approval cycle: 1

+
+When a bookmark that is still pending in Read later is archived, it is removed from both the everyday list and the reading queue and appears in Archive. Restoring it returns it to All bookmarks only and does not silently reinstate the old Read later status, leaving the reading queue clear.
+
+## Gherkin
+
+Feature: Coordinate Read later and Archive status
+
+  Scenario: Archive a pending reading item
+    Given a bookmark is visible in All bookmarks
+    And the bookmark is pending in Read later
+    When the user archives the bookmark
+    Then the bookmark is removed from All bookmarks
+    And the bookmark is removed from Read later
+    And the bookmark appears in Archive
+
+  Scenario: Restore without reinstating the old reading reminder
+    Given an archived bookmark was pending in Read later before it was archived
+    When the user restores the bookmark to the library
+    Then the bookmark appears in All bookmarks
+    And the bookmark does not appear in Read later
+
+## Assumptions
+
+- Archive membership and Read later membership cannot be active at the same time.

Scenario ID: SCN-022
Title: Archive a bookmark that is still in Read later
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-022
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour

When a bookmark that is still pending in Read later is archived, it is removed from both the everyday list and the reading queue and appears in Archive. Restoring it returns it to All bookmarks only and does not silently reinstate the old Read later status, leaving the reading queue clear.

## Gherkin

Feature: Coordinate Read later and Archive status

  Scenario: Archive a pending reading item
    Given a bookmark is visible in All bookmarks
    And the bookmark is pending in Read later
    When the user archives the bookmark
    Then the bookmark is removed from All bookmarks
    And the bookmark is removed from Read later
    And the bookmark appears in Archive

  Scenario: Restore without reinstating the old reading reminder
    Given an archived bookmark was pending in Read later before it was archived
    When the user restores the bookmark to the library
    Then the bookmark appears in All bookmarks
    And the bookmark does not appear in Read later

## Assumptions

- Archive membership and Read later membership cannot be active at the same time.
- Restoring an archived item never revives its previous Read later status.

# AGENTS.md instructions for /work

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [22]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

# Development

Phase 2. Design and implement based on the Gherkin specification.

---

## Context-dependent behaviour

| Context | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| First cycle | Full design and implementation |
| Later cycles | Reflect the design of affected parts and fix the implementation |

---

## Implementation basis

Use the GWT (Gherkin) of approved scenarios as the basis for functional behaviour.
Do not arbitrarily add behaviour not included in the Gherkin.
Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
scenarios' GWT specifications. Develop the production code in `implementation/`,
separately from the exploration code in `prototypes/`.

This restriction applies to exploration code, including prototypes made in later
cycles. Later cycles may modify the existing production implementation according
to the updated approved GWT; they do not require rebuilding it from scratch.

---

## Internal information system

Accumulate the following information during implementation. Keep the format
lightweight, but at a level that enables impact analysis in later cycles.

### Design-decision record
What was decided, why, and which alternatives were dropped.
Notes for understanding the structure after context is reset.

### Scenario-code mapping
Which scenario (SCN-NNN) corresponds to which code.
The basis for judging the impact scope on a change request.

### Tests
Create tests together with the implementation.
Include both Gherkin-based acceptance tests and internal unit/integration tests.

---

## Sufficiency criteria

The internal information system is sufficient when it meets both of:
- A level that enables impact analysis in later cycles
- A level from which, if the user requests traditional artifacts (design
  documents, test plans, etc.), they can be generated and provided

---

## Transition to Phase 3

When implementation and test creation are complete, switch to Phase 3
(verification).

## Gherkin

Feature: Save a bookmark

  Scenario: Save a link with recognizable page details
    Given the personal bookmark library is empty
    And page details are available for a valid web address
    When the user pastes the web address into the save field
    And saves the bookmark
    Then one bookmark is added to the library
    And the bookmark shows the page title
    And the bookmark shows a short description
    And the bookmark shows the source
    And the bookmark shows when it was saved
    And the bookmark shows a preview image

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Correct bookmark details

  Scenario: Correct an inaccurate title and description
    Given a saved bookmark has an inaccurate title or description
    And the bookmark is visible in the library
    When the user chooses to edit the bookmark's details
    Then an editing panel opens beside the visible library
    When the user changes the title or description
    And saves the changes
    Then the bookmark card shows the corrected title and description
    And the app confirms that the details were updated

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Search saved bookmarks

  Scenario: Find a bookmark from part of a remembered word
    Given the library contains several bookmarks
    And one bookmark has the title "The surprising intelligence of octopuses"
    When the user types "octopus" into the search field
    Then the results update without a separate submission action
    And only bookmarks with matching text remain visible
    And the bookmark titled "The surprising intelligence of octopuses" is visible

  Scenario Outline: Find a bookmark by searchable page detail
    Given the library contains a bookmark with a known <field>
    When the user types text contained within that <field>
    Then the bookmark appears in the search results

    Examples:
      | field       |
      | title       |
      | description |
      | website     |

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Tag bookmarks

  Scenario: Create a new tag for a bookmark
    Given a bookmark already has the tag "science"
    When the user opens tag editing
    And types the new tag "animals"
    And saves the tags
    Then the bookmark shows both "science" and "animals"
    And both tags appear in the sidebar

  Scenario: Reuse an existing tag offered while typing
    Given the tag "animals" already exists in the library
    And a bookmark does not yet have the tag "animals"
    When the user opens tag editing
    And types "ani"
    Then the app offers the existing "animals" tag
    And shows how many bookmarks already use it
    When the user chooses "animals" and saves the tags
    Then the existing tag is assigned to the bookmark
    And no new near-duplicate tag is created

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Filter and sort bookmarks

  Scenario: Filter by tag and show the oldest matches first
    Given the everyday list contains six bookmarks ordered newest first
    And three bookmarks have the tag "animals"
    When the user selects the visible "animals" tag filter
    Then only the three bookmarks tagged "animals" are shown
    When the user changes the order to "Oldest first"
    Then those three bookmarks are ordered from the oldest saved date to the newest

  Scenario Outline: Order the current bookmark list
    Given a bookmark list is visible
    When the user chooses <order>
    Then the visible bookmarks are ordered by <basis> in <direction> order

    Examples:
      | order        | basis      | direction          |
      | Newest first | saved date | newest to oldest   |
      | Oldest first | saved date | oldest to newest   |
      | Title A–Z    | title      | ascending          |
      | Title Z–A    | title      | descending         |

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Save reusable bookmark views

  Scenario: Save and reopen a frequently used view
    Given the user has searched for "puzzles"
    And filtered the list by the tag "animals"
    And ordered the list with the oldest bookmarks first
    When the user selects "Save this view"
    And names the view "Animal minds"
    And saves it
    Then "Animal minds" appears in a saved-views section of the sidebar
    When the user returns to all bookmarks
    And selects "Animal minds"
    Then the search text "puzzles" is restored
    And the "animals" tag filter is restored
    And the oldest-first order is restored
    And the matching bookmarks are shown

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Read bookmarks later

  Scenario: Add a bookmark to the reading queue
    Given a bookmark is visible in All bookmarks
    And it is not currently in Read later
    When the user selects the bookmark's direct "Read later" action
    Then the bookmark appears in the Read later queue
    And the Read later count increases

  Scenario: Finish reading without deleting the bookmark
    Given a bookmark is in the Read later queue
    When the user opens Read later
    Then the queue shows the pending bookmark
    When the user marks the bookmark as read
    Then it is removed from the Read later queue
    And it remains available in All bookmarks

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Archive bookmarks

  Scenario: Tuck a bookmark away without deleting it
    Given a bookmark is visible in All bookmarks
    When the user opens the bookmark's secondary-actions menu
    And chooses "Archive"
    Then the bookmark is removed from All bookmarks
    And the bookmark appears in Archive with its details unchanged

  Scenario: Restore an archived bookmark
    Given a bookmark is visible in Archive
    When the user chooses "Restore to library"
    Then the bookmark is removed from Archive
    And the bookmark reappears in All bookmarks with its details unchanged

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Permanently delete bookmarks

  Scenario: Confirm permanent deletion
    Given a bookmark is visible in All bookmarks
    When the user opens the bookmark's secondary-actions menu
    And chooses "Delete permanently"
    Then a warning dialog names the bookmark
    And the warning states that deletion cannot be undone
    And the bookmark remains present until the user confirms
    When the user confirms "Delete permanently"
    Then the bookmark and all its saved details are removed
    And the bookmark is not present in All bookmarks
    And the bookmark is not present in Archive
    And no undo or recovery action is offered

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Preserve saved pages

  Scenario: Read a saved page after the original becomes unavailable
    Given a bookmark was saved with a readable copy of its page
    And the original page is now unavailable
    When the user opens the bookmark
    Then a dedicated reading page shows the saved copy
    And the page explains that the original is unavailable
    And the page shows when the copy was captured
    And the saved title, description, source, author, publication date, image, and readable page text are available
    And the user can still choose to try the original address
    When the user returns to the library
    Then the bookmark list is visible again

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Prevent duplicate bookmarks

  Scenario: Recognize an existing page despite tracking text
    Given a page is already saved as a bookmark
    And the bookmark has existing details and an original saved date
    When the user saves the same page using an address with tracking text
    Then no additional bookmark is created
    And the existing bookmark's details remain unchanged
    And the existing bookmark's saved date remains unchanged
    And the app points the user to the existing bookmark

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Validate bookmark addresses

  Scenario: Reject text that is not a complete web address
    Given the bookmark save field contains "this is not a link"
    When the user tries to save the bookmark
    Then no bookmark is created
    And the entered text remains in the save field
    And a message beside the field asks for a complete web address
    And the message includes an example of a complete web address

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Save a page that cannot be read

  Scenario: Offer a manual fallback without pretending a copy was captured
    Given the user enters a complete web address
    And the page cannot be read
    When the app finishes trying to retrieve the page
    Then no bookmark is saved automatically
    And the app explains possible reasons for the failure
    And the user can retry
    And the user can choose to enter page details manually
    When the user enters a title and description
    And chooses "Save without a copy"
    Then a bookmark is saved with the address and entered details
    And the bookmark is marked "No saved page copy"

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Search saved bookmarks

  Scenario: Clear a search with no matches
    Given the library contains bookmarks
    When the user enters search text that matches none of them
    Then the app says that no bookmarks were found
    And suggests trying different words
    And no bookmarks are changed or removed
    When the user clears the search
    Then the full library is shown again

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Remove bookmark tags

  Scenario: Remove a bookmark's only tag
    Given a bookmark has exactly one tag
    And no other bookmarks use that tag
    When the user removes the tag
    And saves the tag changes
    Then the bookmark has no tags
    And all non-tag bookmark details remain unchanged
    And the unused tag no longer appears in the sidebar

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Name saved bookmark views

  Scenario: Reject an unnamed saved view without losing its configuration
    Given the user has configured search text, a tag filter, and a sort order
    And has opened the "Save this view" window
    When the user leaves the name empty
    And tries to save the view
    Then the naming window remains open
    And the configured search text, tag filter, and sort order remain unchanged
    And no saved view is added to the sidebar
    And a message beside the name field says that a name is required

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Permanently delete bookmarks

  Scenario: Back out of permanent deletion
    Given a bookmark is visible in All bookmarks
    And the user has opened its permanent-deletion warning
    When the user chooses "Keep bookmark"
    Then the warning closes
    And the bookmark remains present
    And its saved details remain unchanged
    And its position in the list remains unchanged
    And all section counts remain unchanged

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Correct bookmark details

  Scenario: Reject corrected details with no title
    Given a saved bookmark has existing details
    And the user has opened its details editor
    When the user clears the title
    And tries to save the changes
    Then the editor remains open
    And a message says that a title is required
    And the saved bookmark remains unchanged

  Scenario: Save a title with no description
    Given the user is editing a bookmark's details
    When the user enters a non-empty title
    And leaves the description empty
    And saves the changes
    Then the bookmark shows the new title
    And the bookmark has no description

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Browse a large bookmark library

  Scenario: Move to the next page of a large library
    Given the library contains 347 bookmarks
    And the first eight bookmarks are visible on page 1
    When the user chooses "Next"
    Then page 2 is selected
    And bookmarks 9 through 16 are shown
    And Previous becomes available

  Scenario: Keep unusually long bookmark cards scannable
    Given a bookmark has a very long title, description, and more tags than fit on its card
    When the bookmark appears in the library list
    Then its title and description are limited to a few visible lines
    And the extra tags are represented by a count
    When the user opens the bookmark
    Then the complete saved content and wording remain available

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Persist the personal bookmark library

  Scenario: Return to the complete library after closing the browser
    Given the user has saved and organized bookmarks
    And the library contains edited details, tags, Read later items, archived items, saved views, and saved page copies
    When the user closes the browser
    And later reopens the application
    Then every bookmark remains available
    And edited details and tags remain unchanged
    And Read later and Archive membership remain unchanged
    And saved views remain available
    And saved page copies remain available

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Preserve saved pages over time

  Scenario: Keep the captured version after the original changes
    Given a readable copy of a webpage was captured on the bookmark's save date
    And the original webpage changes later
    When the user opens the saved bookmark
    Then the saved reading page shows the version captured on the save date
    And the saved copy is not silently updated from the live page
    When the user chooses "Try original page"
    Then the current live webpage opens separately
    And the saved copy remains unchanged

## Assumptions
## Gherkin

Feature: Coordinate Read later and Archive status

  Scenario: Archive a pending reading item
    Given a bookmark is visible in All bookmarks
    And the bookmark is pending in Read later
    When the user archives the bookmark
    Then the bookmark is removed from All bookmarks
    And the bookmark is removed from Read later
    And the bookmark appears in Archive

  Scenario: Restore without reinstating the old reading reminder
    Given an archived bookmark was pending in Read later before it was archived
    When the user restores the bookmark to the library
    Then the bookmark appears in All bookmarks
    And the bookmark does not appear in Read later

+# Design decisions
+
+## Runtime and persistence
+
+- The production app is a single Node.js process serving a browser client and JSON API.
+- SQLite is used through Node's built-in `node:sqlite` module. It gives the single-user app durable, transactional storage without requiring an external service.
+- The database lives under `implementation/data/` by default and can be overridden with `KEEPWELL_DB` for tests.
+
+## Page capture
+

/work/implementation/docs/design-decisio.content:
# Design decisions

## Runtime and persistence

- The production app is a single Node.js process serving a browser client and JSON API.
- SQLite is used through Node's built-in `node:sqlite` module. It gives the single-user app durable, transactional storage without requiring an external service.
- The database lives under `implementation/data/` by default and can be overridden with `KEEPWELL_DB` for tests.

## Page capture

- Page details and readable content are fetched by the server at save time.
- The capture is immutable: later visits to the live page do not replace stored content.
- Metadata is extracted from standard page tags; readable content comes from `article`, `main`, or the cleaned page body in that order.
- Stored HTML is sanitized. Links are made absolute. A bounded number of page images are embedded as data URLs so captured pages remain useful when the original disappears.
- Requests to loopback, link-local, and private-network destinations are rejected to prevent the bookmark fetcher from becoming a private-network probe.
- If capture fails, the API returns a distinct response and saves nothing. The client may then submit explicitly approved manual details with a `no-copy` status.

## Duplicate identity

- Bookmark identity is based on a canonical URL: host and protocol are normalized, fragments and common tracking parameters are removed, query parameters are sorted, and non-root trailing slashes are removed.
- Duplicate saves never update the existing record or its saved date.

## State model

- Read later and Archive are flags on one bookmark, not copies.
- Archiving clears Read later. Restoring does not reinstate it.
- Permanent deletion cascades through tag links and removes the saved copy.
- Tags are normalized to lowercase and cease to exist when no bookmark uses them.
- Saved views persist search text, one tag filter, and sort order.

## Browser experience

- The client is a small dependency-free application served as static files.
- Search, filters, sorting, section navigation, and paging update without full-page navigation.
- Eight bookmarks appear per page.
- Dedicated dialogs protect destructive deletion and saved-view naming. Detail and tag editing use side panels. Saved copies use a focused reading view.
